review_text_raw:
This is a very soft recommend. 

I'm a big fan of the first two games and this phone detective genre as a whole and I was very excited for this game when it came out, but had put it on hold for some other games I was playing and finally got through it this morning. 

Bullet points incoming: 

- The game itself is just okay. The story is serviceable but isn't as compelling as 1 or 2, as none of the characters really stood out. They just mostly served as quick conversation pieces and possible plot points / beats on your journey rather than actual characters. It's nothing bad, but the severe lack of personality from most of the characters is just a bit of a letdown. 

- Gameplay was good, but definitely not as great as previous iterations. I personally didn't mind the more linear aspect of it (sure more puzzles would've been a lot better), but I felt for what it was doing it hit the mark so to speak.

- I know some people missed the horror element of it, but in reality a lot of the horror elements from the first 2 were cheap jumpscares which honestly I'm glad are gone bc that's all they are. Cheap ways to scare you and make you go BOO. That being said, the lack of ambient noise / other creepy subtle things from the first 2 games are also toned way down, to where this isn't really a horror game to me, but more of a mystery / adventure game. I feel going into it in that mindset may help more.

- Also, just curious, why would you remove the fast text option from Simulacra 2 for any subsequent playthroughs? That made being able to replay the game (if you so choose to or to achievement hunt) WAY easier and tolerable since you didn't have to wait for the slow pacing of the texts to come in. Removing that seems like such a huge misstep and is likely the only reason I won't 100% this one like I did the others bc in total reality, this is the first simulacra game where I don't really feel like trying to go back and do it.

All in all, is the game bad?
No, but it's nothing amazing either.

Is it a step down from the previous 2?
Yes.

Is it a horror game?
In my opinion, no. Consider this one more of a mystery / thriller experience versus horror. 

Would I recommend it?
If you liked the other 2 games, I think you'll still at least enjoy your time enough to get through it once. If you don't like the previous 2, you probably won't care for it and I'd skip it. If you're in the middle, get it on sale and give a try maybe. If you don't like it, you can always return it before the 2 hour mark.

review_text_raw:
Simulacra 3, developed by Kaigan Games and published by Neon Doctrine, continues the found-phone horror tradition established by its predecessors, delivering an immersive narrative experience centered around digital mystery and psychological suspense. Set in the eerie town of Stonecreek, the game places players in the role of an intern at a local newspaper tasked with assisting investigative journalist Ruby Myers. The central mystery revolves around the disappearance of Paul Castillo, a software developer whose phone becomes the gateway to unraveling the secrets behind his vanishing. By exploring his digital life through texts, photos, videos, and various apps, players are drawn into a chilling tale that combines supernatural elements with a realistic portrayal of modern technology, creating a sense of intimacy and urgency that few horror games achieve.

The gameplay is built around interacting with Paul's smartphone, where every notification, message, and multimedia file serves as a piece of the puzzle. Players navigate through different apps, decode cryptic information, and use hacking mechanics to access deeper layers of the mystery. The real-time progression of events adds tension and immediacy, encouraging quick decisions that influence the unfolding story. This dynamic storytelling approach allows multiple branching endings based on player choices, enhancing replay value and inviting players to revisit the narrative to uncover all possible outcomes. The interface cleverly mimics a real phone’s UI, making the experience feel personal and immersive, as if players are genuinely investigating a missing person’s digital footprint.

Visually, Simulacra 3 stays true to the series' minimalist yet effective design, presenting a realistic smartphone interface filled with authentic-looking apps and multimedia content. The integration of live-action video calls and interactive elements boosts immersion, while the sound design subtly heightens the suspense throughout the investigation. Despite these strengths, some players have found certain puzzles to be ambiguous or overly obscure, which can stall progression and disrupt the narrative flow. The pacing, while deliberately methodical to build atmosphere, may feel slow to those expecting more traditional horror gameplay or quicker resolutions.

Critical reception for Simulacra 3 has been varied, reflecting its niche appeal. While some reviewers praise its atmospheric storytelling, innovative use of the found-phone format, and the effective blend of horror with investigative mechanics, others point out shortcomings in character depth and the occasional frustration with puzzle design. The player community echoes this division, with many appreciating the eerie mood and unique narrative delivery but expressing disappointment over certain gameplay limitations and the game's pacing. For fans of narrative-driven horror and those intrigued by the concept of piecing together stories through digital clues, Simulacra 3 offers a compelling experience, though it may not resonate with everyone.

In summary, Simulacra 3 represents a strong continuation of the found-phone horror genre, delivering a haunting and interactive story that makes clever use of modern technology as a storytelling device. Its immersive atmosphere and branching narrative paths offer a deep dive into mystery and supernatural horror, appealing especially to players who enjoy investigative and choice-driven games. While some gameplay elements and pacing choices might divide opinion, the game stands as a noteworthy title for those looking to explore a psychologically tense and digitally immersive horror experience.

Rating: 6/10

review_text_raw: I really enjoyed simulacra 1, pipe dreams, and 2 was honestly really cool. But this isn't it. My biggest peeve with this franchise is that it NEVER continues any kind of overarching story, theres never a bigger picture, they always seem to act like there will be but it never happens. The end of Sim 2 made me think this game would be on a large grand scale, a climax involving the simulacras, but it just fell short and the entire game was predictable. I got the best ending on my first try and it was extremely easy to keep everybody alive, and the other games were difficult to get the best ending. I liked that about the other games, it added mystery and replayability. But this game I got the best outcome on my first attempt without any prior knowledge about anything and that is very disappointing to me and makes me have no desire to really go through it all again. The second game was great because it took me at least a few attempts to get the best ending and I remember being genuinely stumped as to what was going on or whodunnit, but I never felt that with this game. Nothing was a mystery to me, I could see everything coming from a mile away. And there was nothing scary either, just a couple cheap scenes with the phones background and that's it. The first two games the background changes throughout and it makes you feel unsettled and its cool to see, but this game just felt... lazy. It feels like the bare minimum and I was really hoping it would be better, but the reason I didn't want to play this game stood true. I feel like i wasted my time with it, but I do hope if they make another game in this franchise, it's better. I really would like to enjoy the series again, but right now, its just repetitive, nothing new happens, its just the exact same situation in each game and nothing in this world they are creating changes. It doesn't feel like the simulacrums are an actual problem, just a minor inconvenience once in a blue moon. I hope the devs read reviews because I saw a lot of people with similar opinions to mine and I would love to see a sim 4 where something new finally develops in this world their building instead of just same shit different day.

review_text_raw:
My partner got me this game on day of release for my birthday and it was an incredible gift.

Simulacra 3 explores lore from the previous three titles and weaves it together in new ways, whilst the previous three show a clear escalation of Simulacra in terms of power and malevolence all the elements of the previous games are here in one form or another.

The game is shorter and I dare say has less replayability than the others, I suspect being developed during a pandemic has had the greatest impact on that. I enjoyed exploring as much of the game in one sitting as I could with frustration only at one part where a button didn't work the first time I tried it and reloading the game I didn't think to go back and try it for another twenty or so minutes - but like I said, that was day of release and easily fixable.

I can understand some of the dissatisfaction with the game as a lot of the cult following of the Simulacra series is having know real depth of knowledge on what a Simulacra is, where it came from, what powers it and other such unknowns where snippets have only been revealed to the hardcore investigators in previous releases within this series. This game starts to lift that veil more during the core story line and so far I have not found any Easter Eggs that hint at it being a false narrative or having further hidden clues. It all makes sense as a story and makes sense with the lore of the previous games, including iconic phrases and moments from previous games that put certain happenings from previous games in a new light.

That said the new mechanics are fantastic, the spooks were great and the characters emotive despite their individual isolation. I had a lot of fun figuring out whose social media handles were what person we read about in the news and the lore. If you love the Simulacra series this is a fine addition with the potential for both expansion and further games in the series. I am excited to see what the devs will come up with next and going for the rest of the endings and achievements.

I liked it, it's an ok - good game according to my taste and if you played any other games in the Simulacra Franchise (like Simulacra 1/2 or Simulacra - Pipe Dreams [free]) or from the Kaigan Games Devs from Malaysia (like their Dr. Who lost Phone investigation game) and liked them, you'll probably enjoy this one, too (can play them in any order you want, as the stories are isolated and not dependent on each other save for a few minor easter eggs and references, etc.)

It's far from perfect though, my biggest criticism would probably be the drove of spelling mistakes in the English language version. It appears as if the later development has been rushed or the translators were on crunch time and there wasn't a single proof reading or QA-testing for the English language version at least, which just baffles my mind.

Has some nice achievements at least but the sped up version for further play troughs from the earlier games is missing.
Also has a little replayability, but there are a lot less choices / different paths & options you can take than the seocnd game still had.

if you liked this, maybe check out Kaigan Games other games if you haven't played them yet:
Sarah is missing, Simulacra (1), Simulacra: Pipe Dreams (free to play and good intro to see if you'd like this paid one, too), Simulacra 2 and maybe Doctor Who: The Lonely Assassins, which is a similar Lost phone / investigative mystery game.

This review includes spoilers: 

I really loved Simulacra 1 and 2 and I replayed them right before the 3. within the last couple of days.
And I've gotta say, I really don't like the main simulacrum in this game. It is way less scary to have a literal monster as the main villain instead of something that possesses humans in my opinion. 

There is also a lack of social commentary, because of that. I've always interpreted the first and second game as social commentaries on smartphone / media addiction. The first one dealt with the negative side of dating apps, the second game dealt with being an influencer and addicted to being famous. This entry does none of that. It's not a social commentary on creepypasta / digital horror, like I thought it would be. 

I also think there are weirdly enough several downgrades in comparison to the 2nd game, which was really weird to me. The UI feels unintuitive, none of your decisions really seemed to influence the people around you, there is no character growth. 

The puzzles feel illogical. Maybe I was too dumb for them, but I don't think the game gives you enough hints to figure out what exactly you are supposed to do at certain points. The hint system was also weirdly useless in this game. 

But I really did like the atlas features (except for the tracing route mode) and the "live" segments.

I'm really sorry to leave this review, I still love this franchise as a whole, but this one just wasn't for me.

As an avid enjoyer of previous entries in the series, I was excited to learn that Simulacra has a third game in its mainline series... but there are reasons why this game has largely flown under the radar. 

Spoilers incoming. 

[spoiler]While an interesting concept, the struggle against the Beldam is significantly less compelling than the simulacra we've seen previously. Characters are unlikable - Ruby is a terrible partner and your options with her feel very linear throughout the experience. The new gameplay elements are a mixed bag: while home security footage segment is cool, the map mechanic was deeply frustrating. None of the missing people you're trying to save are particularly interesting or developed; even Paul (the protagonist). The town in "danger" is literally asking for it for the vast majority of the game. The ending felt abrupt and rushed; the final confrontation with The Beldam lacked the gravitas that previous boss encounters do for the series. To be blunt, I would MUCH rather replay the one with fla-pee bird than replay this game... which says a lot cause I HATED fla-pee bird. [/spoiler]


In many ways, this entry lacks the charm and mystery that makes previous games in this franchise enjoyable.  Overall, I was left disappointed and wanting more from the ending I received - unfortunately, I am not compelled by enough the experience to return to it in search of other endings. I rate it [b]no more[/b] than two stars out of five.

review_text_raw:
Honestly, this game is absolutely nothing like Simulacra 1 & 2. There's not that many routes to take, there's no comedic relief, hardly any relationships between anyone, and etc. It doesn't necessarily feel like a real Simulacra type thing either even though it technically is. This reminds me more of a mix between Sara is Missing and a knock-off Duskwood.

I also struggled a lot with some of the prompts and even had to look up Youtube videos to help me out. For the record, I play a lot of detective-type games like this one, so it's frustrating to find something that's actually extremely difficult when you're used to how the games tend to go.

So yeah, I wouldn't recommend this for anyone who likes Simulacra 1 and 2. BUT, if you prefer Sara is Missing, then this is a more intense version of that game. This one doesn't have the same type of replayable feeling as 1 and 2, even though it is replayable. Just didn't have a lot of enthusiasm and was way too serious for my tastes. It was definitely a let-down compared to the previous versions.

review_text_raw: I have a very mixed opinion about this one I'm teetering between recommending and not recommending and really wishing there was a middle ground, I just played through all 3 games over a two day period so everything is fresh in my mind and I can compare them greatly.  I want to say when I finished number 3 my first thought was "Did I really like this game it was a bit boring"  However, looking at the time in the game, taking maybe a 20 minute break in there, I did not think I spent that long in the game which usually makes me feel like I was quite into it to have that amount of time pass without even realizing it.  Now I bought all three games in a bundle, so I got them all for about the same price 3 retails on its own so I feel I got my moneys worth, however I think if I were to have bought 3 alone at normal price I might have felt a bit ripped off.  I would definitely say I enjoyed the first two games more without any hesitation and have definite plans to replay the first two and try to discover all I missed on my first playthrough, but this one I have a feeling I'll never get around to replaying at least not for a while or there is a lull in new games for me to play, and to anyone new to these games I would recommend playing 1 and 2 first, and then get this one, or buy it on a sale so you feel your getting your money worth.

review_text_raw: I love the other Simulacra games, but I waited a while to play this one because it has mixed reviews. I can understand why now and am disappointed...The game feels rushed. It has typos and the dialogue is poor. Gameplay in terms of finding info and doing puzzles is lame/tedious, and there aren't many puzzles at all. Story and characters are underdeveloped. I was also really disappointed to find your choices don't matter that much throughout the game. There are only a few choices that make any difference in dialogue/outcome, which sucks for a game where 90% of the gameplay is choosing dialogue options. I replayed to get all endings and achievements, but we're talking minor changes between outcomes that make replaying the game basically pointless. Overall, not much actually happens to make the game worth your time. Just skip it if you're a fan of the previous games.
